newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat's Magneti Marelli H1 profit up.
newsitem.headline: Fiat's Magneti Marelli H1 profit up.

text.p: Italian auto components group Magneti Marelli, part of the Fiat group, on Wednesday posted first half 1996 pre-tax profit of 54 billion lire against 32 billion in the first six months of 1995.
Operating profit rose to 79 billion lire from 76 billion while consolidated net income totalled 3.19 trillion lire, up 1.2 percent on last year's first half.
Group net financial debt of 172 billion lire was down 12 billion on end-1995 debt. Investments, equal to over 10 percent of turnover, totalled 337 billion lire in the first half.

Magneti said in a statement that in the context of a market showing signs of a slowdown in vehicle production, "Magneti Marelli has reinforced its own position as supplier to the major world manufacturers, at the same time accelerating action to develop its presence in emerging markets."

It said the group's board had appointed Carlo Camerana as the new chairman, replacing Luigi Francione who has stepped down but remains on the board. Paolo Monferino has joined the board, replacing Umberto Quadrino, and becomes vice-chairman.
